# 0.5.16

## 本次更新

- 修复登录成功后登录页不自动返回首页的问题：自动关闭此前依赖一个可能永远不发生的后续渲染帧，导致用户必须手动点击“完成”才能离开登录页（v0.5.15 生产日志：13:38:23 已确认会话，13:38:39 才因手动操作关闭）。现在所有关闭路径（自动与手动）都会在条件满足时立即执行导航，且保证只执行一次、不会重复弹路由。
- 修复首页推荐整批被丢弃并误显示登录提示的问题：个性化推荐接口（RFY）返回 24 项作品时，应用因历史“通用回退”信号（`vespa_content_group: 2` 游标）将整批内容全部丢弃，首页空白且出现以“登录”为主操作的恢复界面——把推荐能力降级误报成了未登录。现已确认：服务器确认已登录的健康会话同样会返回该信号，其完整协议语义未经证实。
- 推荐疑似退化为通用内容时，内容照常展示，并直接在推荐页顶部显示明确标识（账号已登录、内容未经个性化确认），提供“重试”与关闭；疑似通用批次不会写入个性化缓存，也不会冒充已确认的个性化推荐。只有权威判定网页会话失效时才显示登录恢复界面。
- 网络诊断日志新增脱敏的游标结构信息（仅键名与组号，不含任何值），为后续协议取证积累证据。

## Changes (English)

- Fixed the login screen not auto-returning to the home page after a successful sign-in: the automatic close previously depended on a post-frame callback that may never run while the app is idle, so the user had to tap "Done" manually. All close paths (automatic and manual) now navigate as soon as their conditions are met, exactly once, with no duplicate routing.
- Fixed the home recommendations being discarded entirely with a misleading login prompt: when the personalized recommendation feed (RFY) returned 24 items, the app discarded the whole batch based on the historical generic-fallback signal (a `vespa_content_group: 2` cursor), leaving an empty recovery screen whose primary action was Login — misreporting a recommendation-capability degradation as "not signed in". It is now established that a server-confirmed signed-in session can also receive this signal; its full protocol semantics remain unverified.
- When recommendations are suspected to have fallen back to generic content, the items are still displayed with a clear label directly on the recommendations tab (account signed in, items not confirmed personalized) offering retry and dismissal; suspected-generic batches are never persisted to the personalized cache and never presented as confirmed personalized recommendations. The blocking login recovery UI only appears under an authoritative signed-out verdict.
- Network diagnostics now record a sanitized cursor structure (key names and group number only, never values) to accumulate evidence for future protocol verification.
